185299318.title: File:Paintings of Ayyappan at Shree Dharmashasthagiri Ayyappa Swamy Temple, Huskuru (4).jpg

ImageDescription.value:
A Chitra Sutra painting depicting a scene related to Swamy Ayyappan at Shree Dharmashasthagiri Ayyappa Swamy Temple, Huskuru, Bangalore.

The Queen of Pandalam lies on a couch appearing frail, surrounded by the King Rajasekhara, Manikandan, and a physician. Medicinal jars and a mortar are visible in the foreground.

Specific History: Instigated by a jealous minister, the Queen feigns a life-threatening headache that can "only be cured by the milk of a forest tigress," a plot intended to kill Manikandan.

185299376.title: File:Paintings of Ayyappan at Shree Dharmashasthagiri Ayyappa Swamy Temple, Huskuru (4) (30370).jpg

ImageDescription.value:
A Chitra Sutra painting depicting a scene related to Swamy Ayyappan at Shree Dharmashasthagiri Ayyappa Swamy Temple, Huskuru, Bangalore.

A triumphant Manikandan is shown riding a fierce tigress, followed by several other tigers, as the people of the kingdom look on in awe.

Specific History: To everyone's shock, Manikandan survives the forest and returns to the palace riding the tigress, proving his divinity as the son of Shiva and Mohini (Vishnu).

185299999.title: File:Paintings of Ayyappan at Shree Dharmashasthagiri Ayyappa Swamy Temple, Huskuru (4) (76227).jpg

ImageDescription.value:
A Chitra Sutra painting depicting a scene related to Swamy Ayyappan at Shree Dharmashasthagiri Ayyappa Swamy Temple, Huskuru, Bangalore.

King Rajasekhara and Queen of Pandalam are shown in a palace setting, cradling a newborn baby with a golden bell around its neck.

Specific History: King Rajasekhara of Pandalam, childless at the time, finds the infant abandoned on the banks of the Pamba River and adopts him as his own.
